leftEvidence.title: David’s decay distinguishes him from the raised one

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Paul cites the son declaration and David’s holy mercies, quotes Psalm 16, says David served his generation, died, was buried, and decayed, while the one God raised did not.
points.right: Paul asks about Abraham, contrasts work and trust, then says David pronounces blessing on the person credited righteousness apart from works and quotes forgiven lawlessness and covered sins.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places David’s death and decay become part of a contrast within resurrection proclamation inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places Davidic words enter an argument first framed through Abraham inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: Acts 13:32–39 and Romans 4:1–8 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Gospel and Apostolic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: David speaks of forgiveness in Paul’s Abraham argument

payload.tension: Acts 13:32–39 foregrounds David’s death and decay become part of a contrast within resurrection proclamation; Romans 4:1–8 foregrounds Davidic words enter an argument first framed through Abraham. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
